welcome_lead: It's January 1066 and King Edward has died with no son. Three men say the throne is theirs. Who will win? 👑

walkthroughs.body_html:
On 5 January 1066, Edward the Confessor died in London with no children.

Edward was very religious — he had built the new Westminster Abbey. But he left a huge problem: no clear heir.

The Witan (the king's council) had to choose the next king quickly. ⚖️

Three men said the throne should be theirs:

  • Harold Godwinson — most powerful English earl. He said Edward had promised it to him on his deathbed.
  • William of Normandy — a French duke. He said Edward had promised it to him years before, and that Harold had sworn an oath to back him.
  • Harald Hardrada — Viking king of Norway. He claimed it through an old deal between Norway and England.

The Witan picked Harold. He was crowned the day after Edward died.

Both William and Harald refused to accept Harold.

William started building a fleet on the French coast. Hardrada gathered Viking longships in Norway.

Harold had to defend his country from two invasions at once — and a strange light in the sky (later identified as Halley's Comet) made people whisper that doom was coming. ☄️
